result:
Best laps are now saved per track, the HUD BEST chip shows the saved time, and a NEW BEST chip slides out under it when you beat it. Typecheck, the full test suite (83 files, 621 tests), `check:tokens`, `build` and the screenshot capture all pass. I couldn't check that each AC test fails on `main`: there's no git checkout of the original code here. Going by what `main` does (no storage, no NEW BEST chip, no new stage), each test checks something it lacks.

**What changed**
- **`src/ui/best-laps.ts` (new):** `bestLapKey(trackId)` builds the key `racer.bestLap.<trackId>`. The game reads and writes through a small store that wraps every storage access in try/catch. Any saved value that isn't a positive finite number counts as no best. There's also an in-memory store, used only by the stages so they don't touch real storage.
- **`src/ui/race-ui.ts`:** the race info now carries an optional `trackId`. The BEST chip starts at the saved best. Each finished lap is checked in order, even when several end between two frames. A lap faster than the shown best is saved and starts the NEW BEST chip timer. The chip stays out until lapEnd + ceil((slide + 2000) × 60 / 1000) ticks, slides back, and is gone at lapEnd + ceil((2 × slide + 2000) × 60 / 1000), with slide read from the motion tokens. Starting a new race hides it. The results screen gets this race's best lap plus a new-best flag. With no `trackId`, nothing is saved and NEW BEST never shows.
- **`src/ui/hud.ts` / `hud.css`:** one new element under BEST, built from the same mustard panel class as BEST (no top outline, square top corners), and one method, `newBest('out' | 'back' | null)`. The method only touches the DOM when the state changes, so a frame where nothing changed still writes nothing. The chip only animates transform and visibility, and cuts instantly under reduced motion. TIME never moves.
  - One bug the screenshots caught: putting BEST on top of the new chip made BEST show through the results screen. I fixed it by containing the layering inside the timer stack (`isolation: isolate`), and the results screenshots are clean again.
- **`src/ui/results-screen.ts`:** the chip reads "New best lap" or "Best lap". Either way it shows this race's best, not the saved one.
- **`src/game.ts`:** passes `trackId: track.id`.
- **`src/ui/types.ts`:** updated the `bestLapMs` comment.
- **`src/ui/stages/stage.ts`:** `raceStage` takes an optional `storedBestMs`.
- **`src/ui/stages/new-best.stage.ts` (new):** two stages, `hud` (NEW BEST chip out) and `results` (NEW BEST LAP). I compared both screenshots at 844×390 and 1440×900 against the S1 and S5 mockups.

**Not touched or deleted:** `results.css` is on the spec's file list but needed no change. The spec lists nothing under "Supersedes", so no code was deleted.

**Tests for each AC.** All are new files and use the literal key `racer.bestLap.dust-bowl`, as the plan audit asked:
- **AC1, AC2, AC3, AC7:** `tests/game/best-lap-persistence.test.ts`
- **AC4, AC5:** `tests/ui/new-best-chip.test.ts`
- **AC6:** `tests/game/best-lap-storage-blocked.test.ts` (`getItem`/`setItem` throwing, and reading `window.localStorage` itself throwing)
- **AC8:** `tests/ui/new-best-stage.test.ts`

Two AC tests needed an extra assertion, because the behaviour the spec describes already holds on `main`:
- **AC6:** a race finishing with storage blocked passes on `main`, since `main` never uses storage. The test also checks that the game actually tried to read and write storage.
- **AC5 ("Best lap" case):** "Best lap" plus this race's time is what `main` already shows. The test also checks that the HUD keeps the faster saved best (0:01.00).
